doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

chapter: Johnny Hammond, Dreams and moving to New York
title: The Dreams band and The Stark Reality
summary: He joined the fusion band Dreams via the Breckers, then returned to Boston for Monty Stark's The Stark Reality.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Were Blood Sweat & Tears and Chicago a reason for some of those things?

I think they were a definite reason for Dreams. I think Dreams was a band that was, I mean the guys liked to play that way, but the band was also put together to try to be successful. I mean they saw the success of Blood, Sweat & Tears and Randy Brecker had been in Blood Sweat & Tears and actually left before the band went gold. I mean he did an album with them called “The Child Is Father To The Man,” and then he quit, he said I don’t want to do this stuff, and then Lew Soloff took the gig and Lew was on the famous “Spinning Wheel” record and that went, wherever it went, and Randy could have kicked himself I think. So Dreams was kind of started to try to be a band like that, but it just wasn’t as successful because it was too weird. The horn players were too interesting. The guitar player was completely off the wall, me. The singer was, he was a pretty good singer but he wasn’t powerful like David Clayton Thomas or one of those guys, so the band never really, it didn’t quite know what it wanted to do. And so that band kind of, I left that band and went back to Boston to play in another band with electric vibes and drums, and it was called The Stark Reality, which I’ve never spoken of much in interviews but it was led by a vibes player named Monty Stark, therefore the name The Stark Reality. And Monty had fuzz and everything on his vibes. He was a very creative, interesting guy, still is to the best of my knowledge, and so I’m back and played with them for a couple of years. We made one CD, which was the music of Hoagy Carmichael’s, it was Hoagy Carmichael’s childrens’ music. This is very odd because Hoagy Carmichael’s son, Hoagy Junior, worked at a television station in Boston, WGBH, we all became friends because Monty was doing some music for the television thing, so Hoagy kind of hooked us up with his father.
